description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

AMD is hiring a Distributed Systems Software Engineer to develop, test, and optimize collective communication and networking software for AMD GPUs. The role supports performance improvements across multi-GPU and multi-node AI training and inference systems, collaborating with GPU library, runtime, and ROCm teams.
Distributed Systems Software Engineer developing collective communication libraries and network software, profiling AI workloads and benchmarking GPU systems

Responsibilities:
• Develop & Test Features: Implement, test and debug features in collective communication libraries and network software, under the guidance of senior engineers
• Profile & Analyze Workloads: Profile LLM, diffusion, multimodal, RecSys and generative AI workloads on single-node and multi-node systems, and help identify performance bottlenecks
• Run Benchmarks & Experiments: Run performance experiments across AMD GPU generations and network configurations, and summarize results for the team
• Contribute to Tooling: Contribute to tools and infrastructure for performance measurement, regression tracking and reporting
• Support Model & Framework Enablement: Support new model enablement and out-of-box performance efforts across AI frameworks, and work with internal teams and open-source communities to get changes reviewed and integrated
• Software Engineering Best Practices: Follow sound engineering practices, including code reviews, testing and documentation, to deliver robust, maintainable code
• Learn & Grow: Build expertise in collectives, networking and GPU performance through mentorship, code reviews, knowledge sharing and hands-on project work

Requirements:
• Seeking a motivated C++ developer with a solid foundation in Linux environments, computer architecture and networking concepts
• The ideal candidate completes well-defined tasks with guidance, learns quickly, and collaborates effectively within a high-performing team
• You are comfortable profiling and debugging performance issues and are interested in how AI model architectures map onto software and hardware
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent
• This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship

Preferred:
• Understanding of collective communication concepts (e.g., all-reduce, all-to-all), and familiarity with libraries such as RCCL, NCCL or MPI and with networking fundamentals such as RDMA, NICs and interconnects
• Foundational knowledge of GPU architecture
• Familiarity with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, vLLM or SGLang and with distributed training or inference concepts
• Proficiency in C++ and Python, with experience in debugging, profiling and writing tests
• Strong problem-solving skills, eagerness to learn, and good written and verbal communication skills
• professional experience in software development, with exposure to performance engineering, systems software, networking, or GPU programming
